column1: # Served rows whose scope comes from arguments the client chose, with no server guard (lane L3 S4, Q1-B).
# Per-user access (A1) must not lift while this file has rows; test/rust-served-a1-lock.test.ts enforces it.

column2: hazard
the entity pairs come from the client pool scope; the source grant is not checked and privacy applies only when the client scope carries excludePrivate
the keys and fact pool scope come from the client; privacy applies only when the pool scope carries excludePrivate and the source grant is not checked
the slugs come from the client; privacy applies only when the client sends excludePrivate true, so a private slug is confirmed as a live page without the flag
privacy applies only when the client sends excludePrivate true; the page ids and referrer sources are the client's
the link-note rows are filtered only when the client sends excludePrivate true; the page ids and sources are the client's
the slugs come from the client across sources and the member applies no fact privacy filter, so it returns private claim rows; the recall caller drops them afterward
privacy applies only when the client sends excludePrivate true; the slug and source are the client's, so a private page's type is confirmed without the flag
privacy applies only when the client sends excludePrivate true; the slug and source are the client's, so a private page's rows are confirmed without the flag

by-id form answers for any id the client names (display_name, email, kind, groups): household placement looks up stored reader ids, so it cannot be limited to the caller; the list and email forms are refused
the page ids come from the client and privacy applies only when the client sends excludePrivate true
the source id comes from the client and the coverage event list is source-wide with no caller scope
source-wide history by the client's source id and cursor; the caller filters it in JS after the raw rows return (scanned and lastScannedId cursors), so the server returns private rows too
the source and slug come from the client and the read is filtered only by the privacy and eligibility options the client sends
the source and entity slugs come from the client and the read is filtered only by the privacy options the client sends
the page id comes from the client; with privacy none the entry is returned unfiltered
sourceId and slug come from the client; no privacy or member check, so it answers the title of a private, readers-only or soft-deleted page
page ids come from the client; no privacy or member check, so it answers the title of any page id, soft-deleted ones too
sourceId and the prefix query come from the client; the SQL has no privacy or member predicate, so it lists private pages of the bare-name family
sourceId and the patterns come from the client; no privacy or member predicate, so it lists directories that hold only private pages
sourceId, patterns and title come from the client; no privacy or member predicate, so it matches private pages by title
the source list and the excludePrivate flag come from the client; a call with excludePrivate false groups the private referrers
the source list and the excludePrivate flag come from the client; a call with excludePrivate false lists private records
page ids come from the client; no privacy or member check, so it answers the title and dates of any page id, soft-deleted ones too
sourceIds come from the client (privacy none is served as the caller policy, but the source list is not narrowed); it names live pages of any source the client lists
sourceIds come from the client (privacy none is served as the caller policy, but the source list is not narrowed); it reads pages of any source the client lists
source ids come from the client and the lock variants (FOR SHARE, FOR UPDATE) cross; it answers the config of any source and takes row locks on the brain
sourceId, types and title come from the client; no privacy or member predicate, so it lists the slugs of private pages by exact title
page and chunk ids come from the client; no privacy or member check, so it answers the stored byte position of any chunk
sourceId, slugs and the excludePrivate flag come from the client; a call with excludePrivate false lists private same-name pages
the readable list and the excludePrivate flag come from the client; the answer is one boolean about other sources, and a call with excludePrivate false counts private pages
sourceIds and slugs come from the client; no privacy or member predicate, so it lists private pages that name an entity in text
sourceIds come from the client; aggregate usage counts of any source, no per-caller scoping
the slug and the page policy come from the client; a policy that hides nothing resolves a private anchor to its source
the scan options, with excludePrivate and remote, come from the client; a call with excludePrivate false scans and returns private pages
